titel: AI’s third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers | Tara Seshan (Product Lead ChatGPT Work)

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Tara Seshan on AI's shift toward persistent coworkers and steering over rowing.
kurzfassung: Tara Seshan, Product Lead for ChatGPT Work and Codex at OpenAI, discusses the evolution of AI toward persistent coworkers and agent-driven workflows. She explains how the product management role has shifted from theoretical planning to empirical hypothesis testing and rapid iteration. Additionally, she shares insights on OpenAI's internal culture, the importance of high ambition, and the changing nature of knowledge work.
stichpunkte: AI is moving from chat interfaces to agents and eventually toward persistent coworkers that handle complex tasks collaboratively.
OpenAI operates with a founders-led culture where product teams stay closely tied to research and market demands.
Product management in the AI era requires moving from long theoretical docs to rapid, empirical testing of core hypotheses.
Knowledge work increasingly resembles steering rather than rowing, requiring humans to provide clear direction and taste.
The team relies on internal cultural memes like mainlining the product and constantly asking if projects are maximally accelerated.
Building for AI means focusing on model capabilities expected in two to three months rather than anchoring on current limitations.
ChatGPT Work integrates powerful coding harnesses into familiar chat and desktop interfaces to streamline complex financial and knowledge tasks.
Writing functions best as a tool for thinking rather than reporting, though product mockups and prototypes often replace long documents.

clips.hook: Building for where models will be in two to three months
clips.text: Planning products around the current state of models or looking a full year ahead are both guaranteed paths to failure in the fast-moving AI landscape.

clips.hook: The future of work looks more like steering than rowing
clips.text: As AI agents take over execution tasks, human work increasingly transforms into directing and pointing systems toward the correct overarching goals.

clips.hook: This is the worst the models will ever be
clips.text: Despite their current advanced capabilities, today's models represent the absolute lowest level of performance they will ever exhibit.

clips.hook: Why shipping transformative products beats endless polish
clips.text: Releasing innovative tools early when conviction is high proves far more valuable than spending excessive time perfecting every visual corner.

clips.hook: Testing product marketing fit before writing code
clips.text: Refining the narrative, sales pitch, and positioning with potential users should happen well before any actual software development begins.

beschreibung:
Tara Seshan leads product for Codex and ChatGPT Work at OpenAI (alongside previous podcast guest Andrew Ambrosino, who’s her engineering manager). Before OpenAI, Tara spent over six years at Stripe, where she joined as one of the first five product managers. She went on to lead product for Watershed, which Time magazine named one of the best inventions of 2022, and she is also a founder and Thiel Fellow. Most personally meaningful to me: Tara is one of the three inaugural Lenny’s Newsletter Fellows, a program I ran a couple of years ago to spotlight the most exciting up-and-coming product leaders.

In our in-depth conversation, we discuss:
1. The shift from “rowing” to “steering,” and why human judgment and ambition will become differentiators as AI takes on execution
2. How OpenAI thinks about building for model capabilities two to three months out
3. OpenAI’s best internal memes, such as “Is this maximally accelerated?” and “Are you mainlining it yet?”
4. Why ambition is the new bottleneck for companies, and why elevating others’ ambitions is now the key part of the PM job
5. Writing as thinking vs. writing as reporting
